propositions: The LLM judge exhibits self-consistency drift across repeated evaluations of the same finding, injecting noise into Pass-2 sub-answer vocabulary (Experiment A measures 3-vote agreement over 50 G6/E4/T3 findings using Fleiss κ and raw agreement).

Section-order permutation of input plans can flip gate verdicts (PASS↔BLOCK or PASS↔INDETERMINATE), threatening reliability of criteria routed over multiple re-runs (Experiment B measures verdict stability across 3 distinct section orderings of 14 permutable plans).

Infra-level failures (LLM unavailability, verifier step-budget exhaustion) produce INDETERMINATE verdicts that are execution failures rather than stable judge decisions and must be excluded and re-run.
Self-consistency and order-shuffle pass iff both Fleiss κ≥0.6 AND raw agreement≥0.8; sub-floor results block R5 (Exp A) and R3 (Exp B) respectively.

Re-judging requires frozen, committed inputs (plan texts, finding records) and explicit gate-session context (repo_root, gate_read_root) to make the experiment reproducible without live-store dependency.

The order-shuffle mechanism generates exactly 3 distinct permutations per plan using deterministic pinned-seed shuffling (permutation 0=identity, permutations 1–2 seeded by plan_id) and reorders only top-level `##` section blocks, preserving content.
